author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Capron Park Zoo in Attleboro is mourning longtime zookeeper Kayla St. George, who died at age 39 following a stroke.

St. George had worked at Capron Park for about five years. Her path in animal care included studies at the University of Rhode Island, internships at Mystic Aquarium and Chicago’s Shedd Aquarium, and positions at Buttonwood Park Zoo and Franklin Park Zoo before she joined the Attleboro facility.

The zoo highlighted her commitment to Reeves’ muntjacs, a small deer species native to Asia. St. George served as vice coordinator of the Association of Zoos and Aquariums program that manages the species’ population in accredited institutions, work that connects daily animal care with long-term conservation planning.

According to her family, St. George developed a migraine and numbness earlier this week. Doctors later found a clot near the base of her skull, and she died after a major stroke. Her family has asked that memorial donations be directed to Capron Park Zoo in place of flowers. The zoo said her loss is being felt by colleagues and the animals she cared for.
dek: The 39-year-old animal-care professional died after a stroke, leaving a record of work at several New England zoos and with a threatened deer species.
headline: Capron Park Zoo mourns zookeeper Kayla St. George
